findings.evidence: caption: 'A large, solid, expansive tumor replaced the left kidney' / in-text: 'large tumor of the left kidney' 'consistent with the diagnosis of nephroblastoma of the left kidney'

panels.rationale: Contrast-enhanced CT of 6-month-old boy with incomplete Denys-Drash syndrome shows large solid tumor replacing left kidney, diagnosed as nephroblastoma/Wilms tumor, a canonical DDS manifestation.
panels.attribution_text: Akramov et al. New mutation in WT1 gene in a boy with an incomplete form of Denys-Drash syndrome: A CARE-compliant case report.. Medicine 2021. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000025864. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced CT scan obtained at the patient's age of 6 months. A large, solid, expansive tumor replaced the left kidney. There was no enlargement of lymph nodes, and the right kidney showed no tumor signs.
in_text_mentions: uation and treatment. Abdominal contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) was performed. This revealed a large tumor of the left kidney, combined with malformations of the genitourinary system (Fig. 1). The results of the examination were consistent with the diagnosis of nephroblastoma of the left kidney T3 NH M0. Bilateral abdominal cryptorchidism was confirmed. When the boy was 7 months old, we removed the tumor of the left kidney by open tumor nephrectomy and performed orchiopexy of the left undescended testis. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). B: Right panel is WT1 IHC of same resected tumor; caption and in-text link Figure 4 to Wilms tumor/nephroblastoma in Denys-Drash patient.

panels.figure_caption: HE staining (left) and immunohistochemical staining (WT1) (right) after tumor resection
in_text_mentions: The patient had proteinuria without microscopic hematuria. She underwent a renal biopsy and histopathological examination indicated a diagnosis of Wilms tumor, and then, a right nephrectomy was performed. The pathologic report revealed a nephroblastoma (mesenchymal type) with necrosis based on the National Wilms Tumor Study Group 5 (NWTS‐5) classification criteria (Figure 4). The normal renal tissue structure was clear and demonstrated no evidence of glomerulosclerosis.

findings.label: Wilms tumor
findings.evidence: caption: oval hypodense lesion at the medial aspect of the right kidney with a maximum diameter of 10 mm ; in-text: spherical lesion at the lower pole of the right kidney ... bilateral metachronic nephroblastoma

panels.rationale: Contrast-enhanced CT from a Denys-Drash syndrome case report shows a 10 mm hypodense renal lesion that in-text defines as metachronous nephroblastoma / Wilms tumor, which is a listed manifestation of denys_drash_syndrome in the vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Akramov et al. New mutation in WT1 gene in a boy with an incomplete form of Denys-Drash syndrome: A CARE-compliant case report.. Medicine 2021. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000025864. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced CT scan obtained 8 months after tumor nephrectomy of left kidney showing an oval hypodense lesion at the medial aspect of the right kidney with a maximum diameter of 10 mm.
in_text_mentions: At follow-up after 8 months, a spherical lesion (diameter: 10 mm) at the lower pole of the right kidney was detected in abdominal CT scans (Fig. 2). In view of this new finding, the initial diagnosis was corrected to bilateral metachronic nephroblastoma pT4 NH M0.

plate_findings.evidence: bilateral large lower pole renal masses crossing the midline

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Top-left grayscale LT KIDNEY ultrasound from Denys-Drash Case 2 article showing large lower pole renal mass with central hypoechoic/necrotic components as described in caption; bilateral masses in Denys-Drash infants represent Wilms tumor. B: Top-right color Doppler LT KIDNEY ultrasound showing same large mass with minimal internal vascularity, supporting Wilms tumor manifestation of Denys-Drash Syndrome Case 2. C: Bottom-left grayscale RT KIDNEY ultrasound showing large lower pole renal mass causing mass effect on pelvicalceal system and subsequent hydronephrosis per caption; contralateral component of bilateral Wilms tumor in Denys-Drash Case 2. D: Bottom-right color Doppler RT KIDNEY ultrasound showing large mass with minimal internal vascularity and mass effect/hydronephrosis, consistent with bilateral Wilms tumor in Denys-Drash Case 2.
panels.attribution_text: AL-Amoudi et al. Denys-Drash Syndrome by <i>WT1</i> Gene: Clinical Variability and Management Challenges in Two Saudi Infants.. Case reports in endocrinology 2026. doi:10.1155/crie/8875066. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Renal ultrasound showing bilateral large lower pole renal masses crossing the midline. The masses show central hypoechoic/necrotic components and minimal internal vascularity. They are causing mass effect on the pelvicalceal system and subsequent hydronephrosis (Case 2).
in_text_mentions: Initial renal ultrasound (Figure 4) revealed large bilateral lower pole masses with hypoechoic, likely necrotic centers and minimal internal vascularity. A contrast‐enhanced abdominal CT scan (Figure 5) confirmed the presence of a horseshoe kidney with bilateral heterogeneously enhancing lower pole masses.

plate_findings.evidence: Bilateral cystic, solid lesions in the interpolar region with minimal internal vascularity

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Top-left LT KIDNEY SAG ultrasound from Case 1 Denys-Drash article. Caption attributes bilateral cystic solid interpolar lesions to the figure and describes bilateral enlarged echogenic kidneys with loss of differentiation and left hydronephrosis, supporting Wilms tumor manifestation. B: Top-right RT KIDNEY SAG ultrasound from Case 1 Denys-Drash article. Shows enlarged echogenic right kidney as described; caption attributes bilateral interpolar cystic solid lesions to the figure, supporting Wilms tumor. C: Bottom-left LT KIDNEY SAG ultrasound with calipers marking interpolar lesion. Directly visualizes the captioned bilateral cystic solid interpolar lesion in Denys-Drash Case 1, supporting Wilms tumor. D: Bottom-right RIGHT KIDNEY SAG ultrasound with calipers marking interpolar lesion. Directly visualizes the captioned bilateral cystic solid interpolar lesion in Denys-Drash Case 1, supporting Wilms tumor.

panels.figure_caption: Renal ultrasound showing bilateral enlarged echogenic kidneys with loss of corticomedullary differentiation. Left moderate hydronephrosis. Bilateral cystic, solid lesions in the interpolar region with minimal internal vascularity in Color Doppler Images (not shown; Case 1).
in_text_mentions: Renal ultrasound (Figure 2) showed enlarged kidneys with increased echogenicity and poor corticomedullary differentiation. Left‐moderated hydronephrosis was noted. A complex solid cystic lesion was seen in the bilateral interpolar region with minimal internal vascularity. Similar findings were appreciated on abdominal computed tomography (CT) and renal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI; Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Disease-focused article title Denys-Drash Syndrome + captioned bilateral complex cystic solid renal lesions in Case 1. In Denys-Drash infant this solid-cystic renal mass corresponds to Wilms tumor manifestation from vocabulary. B: Same enhanced CT as panel A showing bilateral interpolar complex solid cystic lesions attributed to Denys-Drash Syndrome per article title and Case 1 caption. C: T2WI panel showing bilateral multiseptated cystic renal lesions in Denys-Drash Case 1, interpreted as imaging presentation of Wilms tumor. D: T2WI panel showing bilateral multiseptated cystic renal lesions in Denys-Drash Case 1, interpreted as imaging presentation of Wilms tumor. E: T1 postcontrast panel showing enhancing septa and periphery of bilateral renal lesions in Denys-Drash Case 1, consistent with Wilms tumor; left moderate hydronephrosis also captioned but not in vocabulary. F: T1 postcontrast coned-down view showing enhancing...

A complex solid cystic lesion was seen in the bilateral interpolar region with minimal internal vascularity. Similar findings were appreciated on abdominal computed tomography (CT) and renal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI; Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Disease-focused DDS article, Case 2 infant. Frontal radiograph shows mass effect from enlarged horseshoe kidney containing bilateral heterogeneous masses described in panel B / in-text as bilateral heterogeneously enhancing lower pole masses, interpreted as Wilms tumor manifestation of DDS. B: Enhanced coronal CT in DDS Case 2 shows horseshoe kidney with bilateral large heterogeneous lower-pole masses, corresponding to in-text bilateral heterogeneously enhancing lower pole masses, consistent with Wilms tumor in Denys-Drash syndrome.

panels.figure_caption: (A) Frontal abdomen radiograph shows central and superior displacement of the aerated bowel loops. Large soft tissue density is noted in the right and left abdomen, which is related to the enlarged horseshoe kidney. (B) An enhanced CT scan of the abdomen in coronal view shows bilateral renal enlargement with cross‐fusion of the lower renal poles, representing horseshoe kidney. Bilateral lower renal poles demonstrate large heterogeneous masses. Right hydronephrosis is also appreciated (Case 2).
in_text_mentions: Initial renal ultrasound (Figure 4) revealed large bilateral lower pole masses with hypoechoic, likely necrotic centers and minimal internal vascularity. A contrast‐enhanced abdominal CT scan (Figure 5) confirmed the presence of a horseshoe kidney with bilateral heterogeneously enhancing lower pole masses.
